text:
carmen: Hi all 1 Had a minor outpatient procedure (knee injection) on 06/14 and claim was processed as denied for 'no prior authorization on file'. Clinic told me PCP said it was fine. Any quick way to get this reprocessed without scheduling another visit?
maya (People Ops): Sorry youre dealing with this. Short answer: request a retrospective (retro) authorization from your PCP, get the auth number and a dated letter, then submit a claim correction/appeal to the insurer with the EOB + auth.
carmen: Does PCP actually issue retros? Clinic said they rarely do them.
pcp-frontdesk: Hey @carmen this is the front desk at Dr. Lees. We can generate a retro referral in many cases if clinical notes support it. We'll need the date of service and the reason for procedure. We normally fax the auth to the specialist and can give you a fax confirmation.
maya (People Ops): Helpful to ask the PCP to: 1) create a retro prior auth/referral with exact date range (e.g., 06/14/2026), 2) include the service CPT code or description, 3) provide auth number and fax confirmation/timestamp.
carmen: What exact info should I put in Anthem's portal? Their free-text box is tiny and I don't want it bounced.
billing-bot: Template tip: include Claim #, Date of Service, Provider name & NPI, Auth/Referral #, and list of attached docs (EOB, PCP auth PDF, fax cover). Upload PDFs. Use Benefits Portal -> Claims -> Correct/Appeal.
maya (People Ops): Here's a short cover note you can paste (works in small fields):

"Requesting claim correction for Claim #<CLAIM#>.
Date of service: 06/14/2026.
Procedure: knee injection (CPT <insert if known>).
Rendering provider: <Clinic Name> (NPI <#####>).
Retro prior auth/referral: <AUTH-12345> attached (PCP fax confirmation included).
Attached: EOB, PCP auth/referral PDF.
Member contact: <phone/email>."

carmen: If PCP gives a fax confirmation only, is that enough?
pcp-frontdesk: Fax confirmation is fine; we'll include the fax header with date/time and a short cover note. If Anthem needs a signed auth letter we can also provide that.
anthem-support: Hi Carmen we can reopen as a claim correction once docs are uploaded. DM member ID + claim # and we'll flag it for manual review. Typical manual turnaround: 7-15 business days. If you paid at time of service, include receipt for potential reimbursement.
carmen: Any codes or reason phrases to include so claims team recognizes this quickly?
maya (People Ops): Use key phrases: "retroactive prior authorization", "retro authorization", "retro referral", and include the auth number. Also include CPT/procedure name. That speeds triage.
carmen: And if PCP refuses to do a retro auth?
maya (People Ops): Then file an appeal with clinical notes and a letter explaining PCP verbally approved or referred. Appeals can take longer and may need supporting clinical documentation from the specialist. We can escalate if Anthem denies the appeal.
carmen: Got it. I'll call PCP right now and ask for a faxed retro auth. Will DM @anthem-support the claim # when I have it. Thanks everyone.
billing-bot: Reminder: Upload supporting docs to Benefits Portal within 30 days of EOB to avoid processing delays.
pcp-frontdesk: We'll prioritize this; please DM your DOB and member ID so we can match records and fax today.
maya (People Ops): If you want, forward the PCP fax image here and I can review before you upload. Happy to help.
